question: The line joining the two focii of a lens is called ________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**Principal Axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The principal axis is an imaginary line that passes through the center of curvature and the optical center of a lens or mirror.**
 
• It is the main axis of symmetry for the lens or mirror, and it helps in defining the focal points.
 
• In a lens, the principal axis intersects the lens at the optical center, which is the midpoint of the lens.
 
• Light rays parallel to the principal axis converge (in a convex lens) or appear to diverge (in a concave lens) at the focal point on the principal axis.
 
• The principal axis is crucial for understanding the formation of images by lenses and mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focal Point**

 
 
• The point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after passing through a lens or reflecting from a mirror.
 
• In a convex lens, it is real and in front of the lens; in a concave lens, it is virtual and behind the lens.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• The distance between the lens or mirror and its focal point.
 
• It is a measure of how strongly the lens or mirror converges or diverges light.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature**
 
 
• The radius of the sphere from which a spherical mirror or lens surface is a segment.
 
• It is twice the focal length for mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Optical Center**
 
 
• The point on the principal axis of a lens where light passes through without being deviated.
 
• It is the geometric center of a lens.
